text:
incident-bot: Pager: genqueue high tail latency (us-west). 90th/99th token latency spiked ~2:04 UTC. Affected: hosted generation endpoints.
elaine_oncall: I’m taking. linking to runbook: https://internal/runbooks/genqueue-latency :wave:
ryan_ic: ETA for initial public note? we should get a brief out within 15m. low risk of data exposure, impact is latency only.
jess_comms: I can draft a short customer-facing bulletin. proposed copy below — please react with :+1: to approve.
jess_comms: ```Public bulletin (short):
We are investigating elevated latency for text generation in our US-West region. Some requests may experience slower responses. Root cause under investigation; no data loss. Next update in 30 minutes or when we have new info.```:eyes:
elaine_oncall: Confirmed: no errors/5xx right now, just increased tail latency. We throttled a noisy tenant to stabilize.
miguel_sre: Adding: autoscaler pulled additional nodes but KV-cache pressure caused slightly longer scheduling. investigating cache eviction patterns.
sophie_support: Heads up — a few customers already opened tickets (IDs: #8212, #8219). I'll pre-post the short bulletin to the support templates channel once comms sign off.
jess_comms: @maya_legal can you quick-check that phrasing (no PII mention) so we can publish?
maya_legal: quick skim — wording ok. avoid naming internal mitigations (throttling) in public copy; suggest we change second line to: "Some requests may see slower responses; we are working to restore normal latency."
jess_comms: Updated: ```We are investigating elevated latency for text generation in our US-West region. Some requests may see slower responses; we are working to restore normal latency. No data loss or security impact detected. Next update in 30 minutes or when we have new information.```
elaine_oncall: +1
ryan_ic: Good. timeline: initial post at 02:10 UTC, follow-up +30m. If resolved earlier, post resolved with root cause summary.
miguel_sre: Quick mitigation note — rebalanced cache shards and disabled one experimental kernel; monitoring latency metrics now.
jess_comms: Publishing now to status page and support-template. Copy pasted to statusboard: 
```
We are investigating elevated latency for text generation in US‑West. Some customers may experience slower response times. Engineers are investigating; no evidence of data loss. Next update: in 30 minutes.
```
elaine_oncall: thanks — notifying oncall rotation.
sophie_support: Posted templated reply to open tickets and set customer watchlist.
incident-bot: Status update posted to public-bulletin at 02:10 UTC.
ryan_ic: Monitoring for regressions. If 99th drops below threshold for 10m, prepare resolved note.
miguel_sre: 02:24 UTC: 99th has fallen ~40% but still above SLO. hold to confirm stability.
jess_comms: Drafting resolved copy pro forma: ```Resolved: We resolved elevated latency in US‑West at 02:32 UTC. Root cause: cache shard imbalance under high prefix reuse which increased scheduling latency. Mitigation: rebalanced cache shards and rolled back experimental kernel. No customer data impacted. If you continue to see issues, contact support.```
maya_legal: wording fine, looks good.
elaine_oncall: Wait for steady 10m window.
miguel_sre: 02:31 UTC: 10m rolling 99th below SLO threshold. confirming one last time.
elaine_oncall: I’m marking incident as resolved. please publish resolved copy and tag affected customers.
jess_comms: Publishing resolved notice now. Posted resolved bulletin and updated support templates.
sophie_support: Notified customers that had open tickets and closed two follow-ups.
incident-bot: Incident resolved at 02:32 UTC. Incident page updated with timeline and mitigations.
ryan_ic: Postmortem action items (short): 1) add cache shard autoscaling alert, 2) review experimental kernel rollout gating, 3) include customer impact examples in runbook. Assign owners in retro.
elaine_oncall: Thanks everyone. brief retro scheduled 2pm PT today. :white_check_mark:
